source.quote: Marantz's own page for the LINK 10n, read 2026-11-24 (the site served its fr-fr locale). Input rows: « Optical input / output (Maximum Support) 2 / 1 (on/off switchable)  44.1 kHz - 192 kHz »; « Coaxial input / output (Maximum Support) 1 / 1 (on/off switchable)   44.1 kHz - 192 kHz » - no bit depth on either. USB-B: « DAC Master Clock Design (USB-DAC) Yes » and « Asynchronous mode (for USB-B input) Yes », with NO rate stated. Network: « Prise en charge de l'audio haute resolution » and « Hi-Res Audio », with no rate. Conversion: « DAC Circuit New MMM-Conversion ». Filters: « Digital Filter MMM-Stream   Filter 1, 2 Selectable »; « Dither MMM-Stream   (Dither 1, 2, Off) »; « Noise Shaper MMM-Stream  Balanced, Natural, Dynamic Music, Dymanic Voice) » - the typo and the unbalanced parenthesis are the page's. No DSD figure anywhere. No prohibition on the page; the terms page was not opened.

facts.chip: No part number: « DAC Circuit New MMM-Conversion », Marantz's own name for its conversion stage, with « MMM-Stream » as the processing ahead of it.

device_settings.why: Four options, named: « Balanced, Natural, Dynamic Music, Dymanic Voice ». « Balanced » is the one to prefer - the other three are voicings aimed at material types, and Auto's job is to deliver the signal rather than to characterise it. The page also offers « Filter 1, 2 Selectable » and « Dither 1, 2, Off », whose effects it never describes, so no value is recorded for those two.

_lusb_est_la_seule_entree_sans_chiffre_e: Optical and coaxial get « 44.1 kHz - 192 kHz »; the USB-B input gets two yes/no rows - « DAC Master Clock Design (USB-DAC) Yes » and « Asynchronous mode (for USB-B input) Yes » - and no figure at all. So the one input a computer uses is the one this page does not rate, and no usb block is written. The device-level 192000 comes from the two inputs that ARE rated and must not be read as the USB ceiling.
_trois_reglages_nommes_dont_deux_indescr: « Filter 1, 2 Selectable », « Dither 1, 2, Off », « Noise Shaper: Balanced, Natural, Dynamic Music, Dymanic Voice ». Three independent settings in the signal path - that is more user control over the conversion than any other mass-market record in this catalogue - and the filters and dither are numbered rather than described. Only the noise shaper, whose options have meaningful names, gets a recorded value. A catalogue that says « set Filter to 1 » without knowing what Filter 1 does would be inventing advice.
